Trestle Freight proposes $182,000 in base salary and a $12,000 signing bonus for Mara to own the internal security platform, with a June 1 start so she can lead readiness work ahead of the July audit.

For the first 12 weeks, we propose two three-day site visits per month, with Trestle covering travel. Mara’s incident coverage would be limited to business hours, with a designated escalation partner handling after-hours coverage. Training that partner and running a handoff exercise would be part of Mara’s onboarding.

Can Mara make June 1 and that travel cadence work? If an earlier start is feasible but would mean leaving compensation behind, we can discuss increasing the signing bonus.

Mara can start June 1 and make two grouped three-day visits per month for the first 12 weeks, with Trestle covering travel. We propose scheduling those visits in advance and keeping the role remote afterward, with any further visits grouped and agreed in advance.

We propose a $190,000 base. Starting June 1 means Mara forfeits a $12,000 vest on June 15. We propose keeping the offered $12,000 signing bonus and adding a $12,000 make-whole payment, both payable on her first payroll. If Trestle prefers to keep the signing payment at $12,000 total, Mara can start July 1.

For the written role scope, we propose naming Mara as the decision owner for the internal security platform’s architecture, including its technical roadmap and design standards. She can lead June audit readiness and train the escalation partner during business hours.

Before recommending acceptance, we need to confirm who will cover after-hours incidents from Mara’s first day, including before the handoff exercise and when the designated partner is unavailable. Can Trestle identify the primary and backup coverage and confirm that Mara’s incident duty stays within business hours?

Trestle can recommend a June 1 start at $190,000 base with an $18,000 total signing payment on Mara’s first payroll. That includes $12,000 to cover the forfeited June 15 vest and $6,000 in additional signing compensation. The signing payment is tied to the June 1 start so Mara can lead readiness for the July audit.

We can put the following terms in writing:

- **Role scope.** Mara owns architecture decisions for the internal security platform, including its technical roadmap and design standards. She leads June audit readiness and trains the escalation partner and runs the handoff exercise during business hours.
- **Travel.** Two three-day site visits per month for the first 12 weeks, scheduled in advance, with Trestle covering travel. The role is remote afterward, with any further visits grouped and mutually agreed in advance.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara’s incident duty stays within business hours from day one. The scheduled incident responder handles after-hours incidents before the handoff. The designated escalation partner takes over after the handoff. A separate backup covers whenever the primary is unavailable, both before and after the handoff. Trestle will provide the names and escalation contacts for those assignments before asking Mara to accept.

Can you recommend the June 1 package at $190,000 base and $18,000 total signing compensation, subject to receiving the named coverage assignments?

Yes. Once we receive the named coverage assignments and escalation contacts, we can recommend that Mara accept the June 1 package at a $190,000 base with an $18,000 signing payment on her first payroll. That payment covers the $12,000 forfeited vest and includes $6,000 in additional signing compensation.

Please include the architecture authority, audit responsibilities, travel terms, and business-hours limits in the written offer as proposed. The remaining dependency is written confirmation of who covers after hours in each phase. Please identify the scheduled responder and backup from day one through the handoff, and the escalation partner and backup after the handoff, with contact details for each.

Trestle confirms the following terms for Mara’s written offer. The named after-hours coverage assignments and escalation contacts are still pending.

- **Start and compensation.** June 1 start, $190,000 annual base salary, and an $18,000 signing payment on Mara’s first payroll. The payment includes $12,000 to cover the forfeited June 15 vest and $6,000 in additional signing compensation.
- **Role and audit.** Mara owns architecture decisions for the internal security platform, including its technical roadmap and design standards. She leads June readiness work for the July audit, trains the designated escalation partner, and runs the handoff exercise during business hours.
- **Travel.** Two three-day site visits per month for the first 12 weeks, scheduled in advance, with Trestle covering travel. The role is remote thereafter, with any further visits grouped and mutually agreed in advance.
- **Incident coverage.** Mara’s incident duty is limited to business hours from day one. From June 1 until the handoff is complete, the scheduled incident responder covers after hours, with a separate backup. After the handoff, the designated escalation partner covers after hours, with a separate backup.

Trestle will provide the name and escalation contact for the primary and backup in each phase in writing before asking Mara to accept.

Ivo proposes a fixed design fee of **$42,500 for 50 guaranteed design days**, discounted from $45,000 if Hearth signs the agreement and pays the deposit within three business days of acceptance. The day allocation would be firm. We can schedule the days in blocks around Hearth’s fabrication deadline.

- **Payments.** $12,750 on signing, $12,750 on delivery of the concept package, and $17,000 on delivery of the final design package. The second and third payments would be due within 10 business days of delivery.
- **Scope and revisions.** Ivo would deliver an exhibit concept, a developed design addressing the agreed accessibility and touring requirements, and a final design package for the fabricator. The fee includes two rounds of revisions, one after concept review and one after developed design review. Hearth would consolidate its feedback for each round. Additional revisions or scope changes would require written approval at $900 per day.
- **Fabrication supervision.** Supervision would be a separate engagement at $900 per day. Hearth and Ivo would agree on dates in advance and approve any travel expenses before booking.
- **Use and photographs.** Hearth could use the final design to fabricate, display, tour, and promote this exhibit. After the public opening, Ivo could show photographs of the installed exhibit in their portfolio and professional presentations, subject to applicable image permissions and credit requirements.

If Hearth needs flexibility on the number of days, Ivo can offer $900 per booked day with milestone billing. Which structure works for Hearth? Please also confirm the fabrication-slot deadline, the date the fabricator needs the final package, and any venue or accessibility requirements that will shape the scope.

Hearth proposes **$42,500 fixed for 46 guaranteed days**, with 44 days for design and two on site for installation. The installation days would cover checking the build against the drawings, advising on accessibility and layout, and preparing a punch list. The fabricator would supervise the crew. Hearth can cover preapproved site travel separately against an agreed cap. What cap would Ivo need for the two-day visit?

**Payment.** Hearth can sign and pay a 20% deposit of $8,500 within three business days of agreement on terms. We propose $12,750 on delivery of the concept, $12,750 on delivery of the final fabrication package, and $8,500 on completion of the installation visit and punch list. Each milestone invoice would be due within 10 business days.

**Scope.** The fee would include the concept, developed design, and a fabrication package with editable source files and print-ready drawings for both the primary layout and an accessible alternate layout. We accept two consolidated revision rounds, one at concept and one at developed design. Additional work at $900 per day would require Hearth’s advance written approval of the cost and schedule impact.

**Dates and venue requirements.** The slot expiry, final-file deadline, installation dates, and venue dimensions are still unconfirmed. Hearth will obtain those from the fabricator and venues, along with access and load-in requirements, and include them in a schedule before signing. Please indicate Ivo’s earliest start and the lead time needed for each design stage, assuming Hearth returns consolidated feedback within three business days of each review.

**Rights and photos.** Ivo would retain copyright. Hearth needs a perpetual license to share the editable files with its fabricator and touring venues, adapt either layout to each site, and fabricate, display, tour, and promote this exhibit. The sponsor’s photo embargo runs through the period between launch and the touring venue’s public opening, expected two months later. Hearth will confirm that opening in writing. From that opening, Ivo may use cleared installation photos in portfolios and professional presentations with the agreed credits.

Ivo can accept **$42,500 fixed for 44 guaranteed design days and two installation days**, with both site dates reserved in the signed schedule. The visit includes checking the build against the drawings, advising on accessibility and layout, and delivering a punch list by the end of day two. The fabricator would direct the crew. Any fabrication supervision would require a separate booking at $900 per day, with dates agreed in advance.

**Payment.** Ivo can accept the $8,500 deposit within three business days and $12,750 on concept delivery. Ivo proposes **$19,450 on delivery of the final fabrication package and $1,800 on delivery of the punch list**, with each milestone invoice due within 10 business days. That keeps payment for completed design work independent of the installation date.

**Schedule.** The earliest start Ivo can offer is the first business day after receipt of the signed agreement, deposit, and complete brief, including venue dimensions, access and load-in requirements, and exhibit content. For scheduling, allow 12 working days for concept, 18 for developed design, and 14 for the final package. With three business days for Hearth’s consolidated feedback after each of the first two stages, allow **50 business days from kickoff to final files**. The two revision rounds fit within that schedule. Please include the fabrication-slot expiry and final-file deadline as separate dates so Ivo can confirm the schedule before signing.

**Travel.** Ivo proposes a provisional **$2,000 cap for one trip covering two consecutive site days**, with preapproved transport, lodging, and meals reimbursed at actual cost against receipts. Once Hearth supplies the site and dates, Ivo can confirm the cap against fares before signing. Any increase would need Hearth’s prior written approval.

**Deliverables and rights.** Ivo accepts the primary and accessible alternate layouts, with editable source files and print-ready drawings for both. Additional work at $900 per day requires advance written approval of cost and schedule impact. Ivo retains copyright and agrees to the perpetual exhibit-specific license Hearth described, including file sharing and site adaptations. Ivo also accepts the sponsor’s embargo through the touring venue’s public opening, with cleared installation photos available for portfolio and presentation use from that opening with agreed credits. Please include a fallback photo-release date in the agreement in case the touring opening is postponed indefinitely or cancelled.

Hearth accepts **$42,500 for 44 guaranteed design days and two consecutive installation days**, with the payment split Ivo proposed. The $8,500 deposit is due within three business days of signing. The remaining payments are $12,750 on concept delivery, $19,450 on delivery of the final fabrication package, and $1,800 on delivery of the punch list at the end of the second site day. Each milestone invoice is payable within 10 business days.

Hearth accepts the proposed scope, revision rounds, editable deliverables for both layouts, and perpetual exhibit-specific license, including file sharing and site adaptations. We also accept the provisional **$2,000 travel cap** for one trip, separate from the fee, with preapproved expenses reimbursed against receipts. We’ll confirm the cap against fares before signing. Any increase requires Hearth’s prior written approval.

For photos, Hearth proposes the **six-month anniversary of launch** as the fallback release date if the touring opening is postponed or cancelled, **subject to the sponsor’s written clearance**. If the tour is postponed or cancelled, Hearth will promptly request clearance for that date and share the sponsor’s response with Ivo. If clearance is still pending at six months, the embargo continues until the touring venue opens or the sponsor authorizes release in writing, whichever comes first. Image permissions and credits apply in either case. Can Ivo accept that provision?

Hearth will confirm the fabrication-slot expiry separately from the final-file deadline and establish what the fabricator needs to hold the slot. The schedule for signature will identify the site, complete-brief delivery date, kickoff, review dates, final-file deadline, and both reserved installation dates. We’ll check that it allows the full 50-business-day design schedule before asking Ivo to commit.

Ivo can accept the six-month fallback if the sponsor clears it in writing before signing. If the tour is cancelled and clearance remains pending, Ivo would otherwise have no date for portfolio use.

Could Hearth secure advance clearance for at least one installation photograph of the primary exhibit, with the image and credits agreed with the sponsor? Ivo could use that photograph in portfolios and professional presentations once the primary exhibit has opened to the public and six months have passed since launch. If the touring venue opens sooner, the agreed permission for cleared installation photos would apply from that opening. Hearth’s proposed embargo can apply to all other images.

The fee, milestones, scope, license, and travel arrangement are agreed, subject to confirming the schedule and travel cap before signing.

Hearth will seek the sponsor’s written approval before signing for **one photograph of the installed primary exhibit**. We’ll ask the sponsor to approve the shot description, credit line, and permitted uses in advance so Ivo can rely on a release date even if the tour is cancelled. Ivo could use a photograph matching that description in portfolios and professional presentations once the primary exhibit has opened to the public and six months have passed since launch, without a second sponsor review. Applicable image permissions would still be required.

If the touring venue opens sooner, Ivo may use cleared installation photos from that opening with the agreed credits. All other images remain subject to the existing embargo. Please send Ivo’s preferred shot description and credit line for the clearance request.

Sponsor clearance is pending. If the sponsor declines, Hearth will bring its response back to Ivo before signing. The fee, milestones, scope, license, and travel arrangement are agreed, subject to confirming the schedule and travel cap.

Ivo accepts the proposed photo terms, subject to the sponsor’s written clearance before signing. Please use the following wording for the request.

**Shot description.** One wide, three-quarter view of the completed primary exhibit, taken from the visitor approach with the space empty. The frame should show the accessible circulation route and the placement of the displays. The exact camera position may vary to suit the installed layout.

**Credit line.** “Exhibition design by Ivo for Hearth Museum. Photograph by [photographer’s credited name].”

**Permitted use.** Ivo may use one photograph matching this description in print and online portfolios and in professional presentations once the primary exhibit has opened to the public and six months have passed since launch. The sponsor’s written approval of this description, credit, and use will cover the matching photograph without a second sponsor review. Applicable image permissions still apply.

The earlier release for cleared installation photos at the touring venue’s public opening works for Ivo. Please share the sponsor’s written response before signing.

Caldera Water proposes a September overlap, with the incumbent remaining director through December and Dev taking over in January, subject to board approval of the appointment.

During the overlap, Dev would lead day-to-day operations and have procurement authority up to $60,000. The incumbent would remain accountable for director-level decisions, and the board would retain personnel decisions through December. We’d ask the incumbent to hand over active contracts, regulatory deadlines, and key external relationships. Dev would lead the operating review and prepare a January priorities and staffing plan for the board.

We can propose a $138,000 annual salary rate during the overlap and $155,000 upon appointment as director. We can also budget up to $8,000 total for temporary lodging, training, or a mix of the two. If a permanent move by September is impractical, we’d consider temporary lodging during the overlap and a January relocation, provided we can agree on Dev’s on-site schedule.

What on-site schedule and relocation date can Dev commit to, and what decision authority would Dev need during the overlap to be accountable for day-to-day operations?

Dev can commit to being on site at both treatment sites in two Monday–Friday blocks each month from September through December, with the first two weeks of September consecutive for the handover. Dev would lead operations remotely between blocks, with a designated on-site lead at each facility. Dev can relocate after the school term ends in December and be locally based by January 1. We’d agree on the block calendar before signing and revisit it if operating needs change.

The $60,000 procurement limit works for routine operations. To own outage response, Dev needs written authority to activate incident command, take equipment offline and authorize restart within approved procedures, deploy crews, approve overtime, and call in approved vendors. Dev also needs authority to make required time-sensitive notifications. For emergency spending above $60,000, we’d agree on a separate limit and a 24/7 escalation path before September. The incumbent would retain director-level accountability and handle escalations, and the board would retain formal personnel decisions.

Dev can accept the $138,000 overlap rate if Caldera covers temporary lodging directly up to the proposed $8,000, with any required training funded separately, and guarantees the $155,000 base effective January 1. We’d put the succession trigger in writing before the overlap starts. The board would vote by December 15, following a joint review of the handover, operating review, and January priorities and staffing plan. An affirmative vote would make the director appointment effective January 1.

If the vote is deferred, Dev could agree to a bridge through January 31 at $155,000, with written authority matching the duties assigned and a firm date for the board’s decision. Dev could defer relocation during that bridge, with lodging covered separately. If the board declines the appointment or January 31 passes without approval, Dev can end the assignment without penalty. Can Caldera commit to the January salary increase and put both board dates in the transition agreement?

Caldera can put both dates in the transition agreement. We can commit to a board vote by December 15 after a joint review of the handover, operating review, and January priorities and staffing plan. An affirmative vote would make Dev’s appointment and $155,000 annual base salary effective January 1. If the vote is deferred, the agreement would require a decision by January 31. The $155,000 rate is contingent on appointment, so we propose a bridge at the $138,000 annual rate through January 31, by mutual agreement, with written authority for the assigned duties and a named director accountable throughout. Dev could defer relocation during the bridge and end the assignment without penalty if the board declines or January 31 passes without approval.

The proposed site schedule works, including the first two consecutive weeks in September, two Monday–Friday blocks each month covering both sites, and a designated on-site lead at each facility while Dev leads remotely. We’d agree on the calendar before signing and review it together as operating needs change. Dev would be locally based by January 1 if appointed on schedule. Caldera can pay temporary lodging directly, with a combined $8,000 cap for lodging and any required training costs, including lodging during a bridge. Before signing, we’d identify the required training and price the lodging against the agreed calendar so Dev can assess the package.

We can put the requested outage authority in writing before the overlap begins. Dev could activate incident command, take equipment offline and authorize restart within approved procedures, deploy crews, approve operational overtime, call approved vendors, and make required time-sensitive notifications. The $60,000 procurement delegation would take effect at the start of the overlap. We propose sending emergency spending above that limit to the incumbent or a designated alternate with spending authority, available around the clock. The incumbent would retain director accountability during the overlap, and the board would retain formal personnel decisions through December.

Can Dev accept the bridge at the overlap rate and the combined lodging and training cap if we settle the calendar and costs before signing?

Dev can accept the $8,000 combined cap if the agreement includes a costed schedule covering required training and lodging for all agreed September–December blocks, with a January bridge allowance priced in. Caldera would pay lodging directly. If Caldera later requires additional training or on-site days, it would cover the associated costs above the cap.

Dev can accept $138,000 through December on those terms. For a full-duty January bridge, we propose $145,000 annualized, with $155,000 effective on appointment and any January pay difference made up retroactive to January 1 if the board appoints Dev by January 31. If $138,000 is Caldera’s ceiling for January, Dev could agree to a limited handover assignment at that rate, with the named director owning day-to-day operations and outage response.

Either bridge would require mutual written agreement after a December 15 deferral. The board would decide by January 31, and Dev could defer relocation until appointment and end the assignment without penalty if the board declines or the deadline passes without approval. Can Caldera take either bridge option to its board?

Caldera can take the $138,000 annualized limited handover bridge to its board. We can commit to a $155,000 annual base effective on appointment, including January 1 if the board approves the appointment on December 15 for that start date.

We propose putting these terms in the agreement both sides take to their boards:

- **September through December.** Dev leads operations at a $138,000 annual rate, with two Monday–Friday blocks per month covering both sites, starting with two consecutive weeks in September. We’ll agree on the calendar before signing. Dev leads remotely between blocks with a designated lead at each site. The incumbent remains director and hands over active contracts, regulatory deadlines, and key external relationships. Dev prepares the operating review and January priorities and staffing plan. The board retains formal personnel decisions.
- **Operating authority.** Dev has written authority from the start of the overlap to spend up to $60,000 and carry out the outage response duties we discussed. Before September, we’ll name the incumbent and an alternate for 24/7 escalation and document who can approve emergency spending above $60,000.
- **Lodging and training.** Before signing, we’ll agree on a costed schedule within the $8,000 combined cap covering required training, lodging for every agreed September–December block, and a January lodging allowance for the limited bridge. Caldera pays lodging directly. If Caldera requests additional training or on-site days, we’ll agree on the scope and cost in writing before adding them, using the remaining budget or adjusting the schedule by mutual agreement.
- **Appointment and bridge.** The board votes by December 15 after a joint review of the transition deliverables. If it approves, Dev is locally based and starts as director on January 1. If it defers, a bridge requires mutual written agreement and the board must decide by January 31. During the bridge, Dev supports the handover and the named director owns day-to-day operations and outage response. Dev may defer relocation until appointment and end the assignment without penalty if the board declines or January 31 passes without approval.

Can Dev take that package to its board, including the proposed process for any training or on-site days added after signing?

Yes. Dev can take the package to its board, including the $138,000 annualized rate for a mutually agreed January bridge limited to handover support. The written agreement should name the director who will own day-to-day operations and outage response during that bridge and confirm the $155,000 base effective on appointment.

The proposed process for added training or on-site days works. Before signing, we’ll confirm that the $8,000 budget covers the agreed September–December lodging, required training, and January bridge lodging allowance. Later additions require mutual written agreement on scope and cost. If an addition would exceed the cap, Caldera can fund the difference or both sides can agree to revise the schedule. Until then, the agreed schedule governs.

Noor proposes starting the methods desk at three days per week through February and moving to four days on March 1. At a full-time annual salary of $125,000, that would mean annual pay rates of $75,000 and $100,000, respectively. In the first phase, Noor would establish the desk’s standards and handle priority reviews. The fourth day would add capacity for routine reviews and staff training.

Noor’s existing editorial project will continue independently for its remaining nine months. Its data and unfinished articles would stay outside Finch’s assignment of rights. If Finch covers work involving that project, Noor would disclose the overlap and recuse. Finch would designate another editor to handle the review and any correction in that case.

For other Finch work, Noor would have final editorial authority over whether a methods correction is warranted and what it says, after consulting the responsible editor. We’re flexible on title and propose a late-February review to agree on priorities for the fourth day, with the schedule and pay increase set at signing. Would that division of authority work for Finch, and which desk duties would you prioritize during the three-day phase?

Finch can work with Noor on a three-day schedule through February if the desk can receive and triage submissions four days a week starting in December. A deputy would cover the fourth day. We propose agreeing at signing on a written process that defines what the deputy can handle independently, what gets logged and handed off to Noor, and what needs immediate escalation to the editor-in-chief.

During the first phase, Noor’s priorities would be setting the desk’s standards, handling priority reviews, and training the deputy to triage submissions and conduct routine reviews. With deputy training as part of the role, Finch proposes a $128,000 full-time salary basis, prorated to annual pay rates of $76,800 at three days and $102,400 at four days. We can fix the March 1 schedule and pay increase at signing and use the late-February review to set priorities for Noor’s fourth day.

Finch can agree to keep the existing project’s data and unfinished articles outside its assignment of rights, with separate materials and workspaces. Noor would disclose overlaps and recuse, and Finch would assign another editor to lead the review and handle any correction.

For other Finch work, Noor would lead the methods assessment and recommend whether to issue a correction and how to word it after consulting the responsible editor. If they disagree, both views go to the editor-in-chief, who makes the final decision on whether to publish a correction and its wording.

Could Noor take on deputy training within the three-day schedule if the deputy owns fourth-day intake and routine triage?

Yes. Noor can train the deputy within the three-day schedule. From December, the deputy would own fourth-day intake and triage, conduct routine reviews under the agreed standards, and log priority cases for Noor’s next scheduled day. The written process can direct the deputy to escalate urgent concerns to the editor-in-chief, who could pause publication pending Noor’s assessment. That gives Finch four days of coverage without requiring Noor to be on call.

Noor accepts the $128,000 full-time salary basis, the prorated annual rates of $76,800 and $102,400, and the March 1 increase fixed at signing. The late-February review can set priorities for the fourth day. The proposed rights and recusal terms also work, with the appointment expressly allowing Noor to continue directing the independent project through completion.

The remaining issue is who decides a disputed methods correction. We propose that the responsible editor can ask Noor to reconsider and that the editor-in-chief can convene a prompt review of both views. After that review, Noor would have final say on whether a methods correction is required and on its substantive wording. Finch would publish the correction and retain control of placement and presentation. For matters where Noor recuses, Finch’s designated editor would handle the decision. Can Finch agree to that division of authority?

Finch needs the editor-in-chief to retain final authority over whether to publish a disputed correction and its substantive wording. Noor would lead the methods assessment and draft the proposed correction. The responsible editor could request reconsideration, and if disagreement remains, the editor-in-chief would promptly review both views, consult Noor before making any substantive changes, and record the decision and rationale in the desk’s correction log. When Noor recuses, Finch’s designated editor would take Noor’s place in that process.

The other appointment terms are agreed, including Noor’s ability to direct the independent project through completion. Can Noor agree to this correction process so we can put the terms in writing?

Noor needs final say on the desk’s methods finding and the wording that conveys it to readers. Could Finch use a signed methods note when disagreement persists after reconsideration?

Under that arrangement, Noor would decide whether a methods error requires correction and write the note explaining what was wrong and how it affects the article. Finch would publish the note as written and link it from the article. The editor-in-chief would retain final authority over whether to issue a separate Finch correction and what it says, including any disagreement with the desk’s finding. Both views and the rationale would go in the correction log.

The publication commitment is essential to Noor. Readers would see the desk’s finding even if the editor-in-chief declined a separate correction. Finch’s designated editor would take Noor’s place in recusal cases. If Finch can commit to that process, Noor is ready to put the agreed package in writing.

Finch can make a signed methods note the default when disagreement persists after reconsideration. Noor would have final say on the desk’s finding and would approve the wording of any note published under Noor’s name. The editor-in-chief would make a prompt decision on publication. If approved, Finch would publish the signed note and link it from the article, whether or not Finch issues a separate correction.

If the editor-in-chief asks for changes Noor declines or decides to withhold the note, the correction log would preserve Noor’s original text, both views, and the editor-in-chief’s reasons. The editor-in-chief would also retain final authority over any separate Finch correction. In recusal cases, the designated editor would take Noor’s place in this process.

Can Noor accept publication as the default with that final review?

Noor could accept final review if it can delay publication for a defined reason. An indefinite veto over the signed note would leave readers without the desk’s finding.

Could we agree that Finch will publish and link Noor’s signed note within five working days of reconsideration? The editor-in-chief could request changes during that period. If Noor stands by the text, Finch would publish it as written and could publish its own response alongside it. A specific legal or source-confidentiality concern could justify holding the affected passage. Finch would record the reason, and Noor would approve wording that communicates the finding while protecting the source or addressing the legal concern.

The editor-in-chief would retain final say over any separate Finch correction. If Finch needs discretion to withhold the desk’s finding solely because of an editorial disagreement, Noor can’t accept the appointment on those terms.

Finch can commit to a decision within five working days after reconsideration. Publication of the signed note would be the default, and the editor-in-chief could publish a response alongside it. Noor would control the desk’s finding and approve any wording published under Noor’s name. If a legal or source-confidentiality concern affects only part of the note, we would work with Noor to clear and publish the rest within that window.

The editor-in-chief must retain the final decision on publishing the signed note as well as any separate Finch correction. If the editor-in-chief withholds either, Finch would give Noor the specific reasons in writing within the same five-day window and preserve Noor’s finding and both views in the correction log.

That leaves a gap on the term Noor has identified as essential. If publication over the editor-in-chief’s objection is a condition of the appointment, we don’t have an agreement.

We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

1. **Purpose and access.** The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare, perform and report the vibration tests specified in the agreed test plan. Access is limited to test personnel listed by name in a schedule approved in writing by the Design Owner. Personnel may be added or replaced by email approval before access begins. Each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House remains responsible for their compliance. Adviser status alone confers no access.

2. **Working copies and fixtures.** Listed personnel may make the working copies reasonably needed for the tests. Digital copies must be encrypted in transit and at rest. Personnel may extract only the geometry needed to design and fabricate fixtures for these tests. The Testing House must protect fixture files and physical fixtures from access by others. It may not reuse the drawings, geometry, fixture files or fixtures for another project or use them to develop or assist anyone in developing a competing product.

3. **Acceptance and destruction.** Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the test engagement, the Testing House must securely erase the supplied files, working copies and fixture files, and destroy physical fixtures incorporating the geometry. The Testing House may retain the accepted report and test measurements provided they do not disclose or permit reconstruction of the CAD geometry.

4. **Verification.** By the same deadline, the Testing House must provide a signed certificate from an independent verifier identifying the materials covered, the destruction methods and completion dates, and confirming completion. The verifier may rely on deletion records and witnessed fixture destruction without receiving the CAD files. This certification replaces on-demand site access.

Can your test systems meet the 30-day deadline, including for backups? If a backup or record-retention obligation requires an exception, please identify the material affected, who could access it and the shortest retention period you can commit to.

We can commit to the 30-day deadline for active files, specialist copies and fixtures. We propose keeping drawing-bearing material out of routine backups from the outset. We would confirm the backup settings for each recipient before releasing any geometry. Our two-year calibration records can be kept without geometry.

We accept the proposed purpose, confidentiality, encryption and reuse restrictions. We propose the following amendments.

1. **Access schedule.** “Before release, the parties shall approve by email a schedule identifying each recipient organisation, its named personnel, its task and the material it may receive. The machining shop may receive only the isolated extract needed to fabricate the fixture. The accredited lab may receive only the test instructions and any isolated extract needed for setup or measurement. The Testing House remains responsible for both specialists.”

2. **Specialist substitution.** “The Testing House may propose a replacement by email, identifying the same schedule details and confirming equivalent confidentiality and security controls and, for a replacement lab, applicable accreditation. The Design Owner shall approve or give reasonable grounds for objection within two business days. The replacement shall receive material only after email approval. On changeover, the Testing House shall revoke the outgoing specialist’s access and obtain written confirmation of deletion or return of its copies.” We can also list an approved alternate in the initial schedule and activate it by email notice if its personnel, task and permitted extract remain as approved.

3. **Handling and retention schedule.** “Before release, the Testing House shall confirm that each recipient can confine drawing-bearing files and extracts to storage excluded from routine backups. Any necessary exception requires prior written agreement in the schedule identifying the material, authorised recovery personnel, fixed expiry and deletion procedure following restoration. The Testing House may retain geometry-free calibration records for two years from the relevant test date, accessible only to authorised quality personnel and auditors responsible for calibration verification.” We accept the proposed treatment of the report and measurements. To give destruction a definite trigger, we propose that the report be deemed accepted **for destruction purposes only** if the Design Owner raises no specific written objection within 15 business days of delivery.

4. **Verification.** “By the 30-day deadline, the Testing House’s quality manager shall sign a certificate identifying the scheduled materials by reference, the deletion or destruction methods and dates, and any expressly permitted retention. The Testing House shall obtain a corresponding attestation from each specialist and record the witnessed destruction of each fixture incorporating the geometry. If the Design Owner identifies a specific discrepancy, the Testing House shall provide relevant redacted records. If the discrepancy remains unresolved, a mutually agreed independent verifier may review those records remotely under confidentiality. Verification confers no right of entry to a shared customer site.”

Would the specialist attestations and witnessed fixture-destruction records meet your verification requirement if independent review remains available for an unresolved discrepancy?

Yes. We accept the quality manager’s certificate, each specialist’s attestation and the witnessed fixture-destruction records as proof of destruction. We agree to remote review without site access. To ensure either party can resolve a discrepancy, we propose replacing the independent-review sentence with this wording.

> Before release, the parties shall name an independent verifier by email. If the Design Owner identifies a specific discrepancy that the redacted records do not resolve, the Design Owner may refer it to the verifier. The Testing House shall provide, and shall require each affected specialist to provide, the records needed for remote review under confidentiality. The verifier shall report its findings to both parties. If it identifies an outstanding deletion or destruction obligation, the Testing House shall complete it and provide a corrected certificate with supporting attestations.

We accept the access schedule, the two-business-day response period and activation of a preapproved alternate by email notice within its approved scope. We also accept the backup controls, the two-year retention of geometry-free calibration records and the 15-business-day review period. To cover a timely objection and any agreed backup exception, we propose adding the following.

> If the Design Owner raises a specific written objection within the review period, the 30-day destruction period begins on written acceptance or, for destruction purposes only, after a further 15 business days from delivery of a revised report addressing the objection, unless the Design Owner raises a specific written objection within that period. Earlier termination starts the 30-day period regardless of report status. If an approved backup exception extends beyond the certificate date, the certificate shall identify the retained material and its agreed expiry. The Testing House shall provide a supplemental attestation confirming deletion within five business days after that expiry.

With those additions, we can agree to the proposed amendments.

We accept both passages as proposed. They complete our agreement on the access schedule, the handling and retention schedule, and verification. Before releasing any geometry, we will confirm each recipient’s backup controls and agree both schedules and the independent verifier with you by email.

We propose a narrow exception for confidential review. Could you authorize access for four festival programmers and one outside accessibility reviewer, all bound by confidentiality and limited to their assigned review? Two programmers need offline access on encrypted equipment. We can limit that to one copy each, prohibit onward sharing, and delete those copies once their review is complete. We can revoke platform access when review closes. The platform may retain a restricted backup for up to 30 days after removal, so the agreement would need to allow that retention.

The selection board also needs to hear a short synopsis in closed session. We can use a synopsis you approve in advance and keep the screener limited to the five reviewers.

If the film is selected, we’d like permission for the catalog team to draft the entry confidentially. We can send you the draft for approval and hold publication until the agreed announcement date, even if the film’s public release comes later. Could you confirm which of these permissions you can grant and flag any that require separate approval?

We can agree to a narrow written exception for confidential review by four named festival programmers and one named outside accessibility reviewer. Please send their names and roles before access is issued. Each reviewer must be bound by confidentiality, use an individually watermarked screener solely for their assigned review, and refrain from onward sharing or copying except as expressly permitted below.

- **Offline review.** We can authorize one individually watermarked copy each for the two designated programmers, stored on encrypted equipment. Each copy must be deleted when that programmer finishes reviewing, or promptly upon withdrawal of the cut or closure of review, whichever comes first. Please confirm how quickly you can complete deletion on withdrawal and provide a record identifying the reviewer, cut, and deletion date.
- **Withdrawal and backups.** The producer may withdraw or replace a cut at any time. On notice, the festival must immediately disable platform access and direct reviewers to stop viewing and delete their offline copies. A replacement cut requires fresh authorization. We can allow a restricted platform backup for up to 30 days from removal, provided it is inaccessible to reviewers, retained solely for disaster recovery, and purged by day 30. If the platform restores a backup during that window, the withdrawn cut must remain inaccessible and the original purge deadline must still apply. Please confirm the platform can enforce those conditions.
- **Selection board.** The board may hear a short, producer-approved synopsis in closed session, with attendees bound by confidentiality. The board receives no screener access. The synopsis must omit the ending and the cast cameo.
- **Catalog and announcement.** If selected, designated catalog staff may draft the entry confidentially using producer-supplied or approved materials. We can clear draft copy within two business days of receipt. Any publicity excerpt, still, or clip requires separate written approval. The ending and cameo must stay out of all festival publicity.

For approved publicity, the embargo should lift only at the announcement date, time, and time zone we both confirm in writing, and only for the exact materials the producer has approved. That announcement can precede public release. If we have yet to agree on the announcement timing or approve the materials, hold publication. Withdrawal of a cut before announcement also puts any publicity based on that cut on hold pending written reconfirmation.

To finalize the exception, we need the reviewer names, the offline deletion turnaround and backup confirmation, and the proposed announcement timing. The board synopsis and each publicity item remain subject to the approvals above.

We can proceed on those terms, subject to the confirmations below. We’ll send the names and roles of the four programmers and the outside accessibility reviewer, identify the two offline users, and bind all five to confidentiality before issuing individually watermarked screeners.

On withdrawal, we’ll immediately disable platform access and instruct reviewers to stop viewing. We propose a 24-hour maximum from notice for offline deletion, subject to confirming that both designated programmers can meet it before either copy is issued. Each copy must also be deleted when its reviewer finishes or when review closes, whichever comes first. We’ll provide a deletion record identifying the reviewer, cut, and deletion date. Any replacement cut requires fresh written authorization.

Platform confirmation is still pending. Before uploading the cut, we’ll verify that backups are restricted to disaster recovery, inaccessible to reviewers, and purged within 30 days of removal. We’ll also verify that a restore preserves both the access block and the original purge deadline. If the platform cannot meet those conditions, we’ll propose an alternative for written approval before uploading.

Please send the short synopsis you approve for the closed selection board session, with the ending and cameo omitted. Board attendees will be bound by confidentiality, and screener access will stay with the five reviewers.

If selected, designated catalog staff will draft confidentially from producer-supplied or approved materials. We’ll submit the exact copy for approval at least two business days before the proposed announcement and seek separate written approval for each excerpt, still, or clip. All publicity will omit the ending and cameo. The announcement date, time, and time zone are still open. We’ll propose them once the festival schedule is confirmed and hold publication until we have written agreement on timing and approval of the exact materials. If a cut is withdrawn before announcement, publicity based on it will stay on hold pending written reconfirmation.

Agreed on the 24-hour maximum for offline deletion after withdrawal. Before either offline copy is issued, please confirm both designated programmers can meet that deadline. The earlier deletion triggers still apply, and we’ll need a deletion record for each copy.

Please send the reviewer names and roles and identify the two offline users. Hold the upload until you confirm the platform can meet the backup and restore conditions, or we approve an alternative in writing.

Please send a proposed short synopsis for producer approval. Omit the ending and cameo and hold it from the board until we approve the exact text in writing.

The catalog workflow is agreed. Publication remains on hold until we agree in writing on the announcement date, time, and time zone and approve the exact materials. Each excerpt, still, or clip requires separate written approval. If we withdraw the cut before announcement, publicity based on it stays on hold pending written reconfirmation.

Please send a brief premise and any plot points we may use. We’ll draft a short synopsis that omits the ending and cameo, and hold it from the board until you approve the exact text in writing.

We’ll send the four programmers’ names and roles and the outside accessibility reviewer’s name and role before issuing access. We’ll identify the two offline users and confirm that both can delete their copies within 24 hours of withdrawal before issuing either copy. We’ll provide a deletion record for each copy identifying the reviewer, cut, and deletion date. The upload remains on hold until we verify the platform’s backup and restore controls or you approve an alternative in writing.

We’ll propose the announcement date, time, and time zone once the festival schedule is confirmed. Publication remains on hold pending written agreement on timing and written approval of the exact materials, including separate approval for each excerpt, still, or clip. If the cut is withdrawn before announcement, publicity based on it will require written reconfirmation.

We’ll supply a producer-cleared premise and any plot points you may use once we’ve cleared them for the board. Until then, please leave the synopsis off the board agenda. Once you have those materials, send us the exact proposed text for written approval before the closed session.

messages.text:
We propose replacing the blanket approval requirement with these terms for the three-depot trial.

1. Raw failure traces and firmware parameters may be accessed only by designated trial-team members who need them for diagnosis and are bound to confidentiality. An external maintenance contractor receives fault summaries and repair instructions by default. What maintenance decision, if any, requires the contractor to inspect a raw trace? If summaries are insufficient, we can agree in writing to add named technicians to the trial team with access limited to the relevant traces for that task.

2. Either party may publish trial-wide aggregate uptime, pooled across all three depots, without route or depot identifiers or detail that would reasonably reveal either. Before releasing an external trial report, the publishing party will give the other party 10 working days to review the draft. The reviewer must identify any protected material or factual error with specificity. The publisher will remove protected material and correct verified errors. Once the review period expires, either party may publish qualifying aggregate uptime without further approval. Other trial measurements require written agreement before external release.

3. Either party may immediately disclose the minimum information needed to address an urgent safety risk to those able to act on it. The disclosing party will notify the other as soon as practicable afterward, identifying what it shared, with whom, and why.

We can agree to trial-wide uptime publication after a 10-working-day review and immediate disclosure for urgent safety risks, with the following terms for the three-depot trial.

1. **Maintenance.** Give designated contractor technicians fault summaries and repair instructions under written confidentiality and use restrictions. A short trace excerpt may be needed when the sequence of an intermittent fault determines whether to replace the sensor or repair its connection. At kickoff, both parties’ trial leads can approve a roster of technicians eligible to receive excerpts. For each repair, the operator’s maintenance lead will record why the summary is insufficient and limit access to the relevant excerpt for the duration of the repair. Strip exact depot and clock-time information from the excerpt while preserving relative timing. Full traces and firmware parameters remain restricted to designated trial-team members. Any contractor access beyond the approved excerpts requires both trial leads’ written agreement.

2. **Monthly board reporting.** The operator’s trial lead will send the maker’s trial lead a draft of the pooled three-depot report five working days before it goes to the transit board. The report will cover uptime, total device failures, and repairs completed. The maker may flag specific confidentiality issues or factual errors during that window. The operator will remove protected material and correct verified errors, then circulate the report to the board under applicable confidentiality safeguards without further approval. Any portion intended for a public meeting or public board packet follows the publication terms below, subject to legally required disclosures.

3. **Publication.** Each party’s designated publication lead may approve its own external release of qualifying pooled uptime after giving the other party 10 working days to review the draft. The publisher will remove protected material and correct verified errors. Both board reports and public releases will omit depot and route identifiers, exact timestamps, and small counts or other details that could reasonably identify an employee or depot. External release of any other trial measurements requires written approval from both publication leads, subject to the disclosure exceptions below.

4. **Safety and required disclosures.** Either party may share the minimum information needed with authorities, emergency responders, or others able to act on an urgent safety risk. Either party may also make a legally required disclosure within the applicable deadline, including prompt reporting of a serious incident to the responsible authority. Neither disclosure requires advance notice or approval. Exact location or time may be included when necessary for response or required reporting. The disclosing party will tell the other as soon as practicable afterward, where legally permitted, what it shared, with whom, and why.

Can you agree to the preapproved technician roster and five-working-day board review on that basis?

Yes. We agree to the four terms as drafted. Joint approval of the kickoff roster designates the listed technicians as trial-team members solely for access to repair-specific excerpts. Once the maintenance lead records why a summary is insufficient, a rostered technician may inspect the relevant excerpt for the duration of the repair without a second approval. Roster membership alone grants no access to full traces or firmware parameters.

We accept five working days for review of the confidential monthly board report covering pooled uptime, total device failures, and completed repairs. Either party may publish qualifying pooled uptime after the 10-working-day review. Voluntary public release of failure or repair counts, including in a public board packet, requires both publication leads’ written approval. The urgent safety and legally required disclosure exceptions apply as drafted.

We propose limiting subcontractor access to one named color specialist, subject to the archive’s prior written approval. The specialist would have view-only access to first-batch master images in a secure workspace for up to three business days, under written confidentiality and use restrictions. Downloads, local copies, and onward sharing would be disabled. We’d revoke access as soon as calibration is complete. Full frames help the specialist assess color across the page. If the archive prefers to keep the masters in-house, we can provide color-target captures and crops selected with the archive, then apply the calibration ourselves.

We’d give the archive ten calendar days after delivery to flag scan defects and would deliver corrections within ten calendar days of receiving them. We’d delete working copies within two business days after that review window closes or the last timely correction is delivered, whichever is later. Existing backups would age out within 45 calendar days of working-copy deletion. Until then, they’d be restricted to disaster recovery, with the same deletion requirement reapplied if restored. We’d confirm working-copy deletion and final backup expiry in writing.

We’d also like permission to publish one anonymized image of the scanning setup. We can stage it with a blank sheet so no donor material appears. We’d submit the exact image and caption for written approval before publication.

We can agree to the calibration alternative. For two collections, only archive personnel may view handwriting or identifying content. We’ll identify those collections before transfer. We’ll supply a calibration sheet that the specialist may assess in full frame. If the specialist also needs examples from actual scans, we can approve masked images from other collections after checking that the masking conceals identifying content. The studio would apply the calibration. We accept the proposed controls for one named specialist, with archive approval in writing before access and revocation on completion or after three business days, whichever comes first. Please confirm the studio can process the two restricted collections without staff viewing protected content. If a step requires visual inspection, reserve it for archive personnel.

We accept the ten-calendar-day defect review and correction periods and the two-business-day deletion deadline for working copies, including temporary files and specialist previews. We propose a backup limit of 30 calendar days from working-copy deletion, with access restricted to disaster recovery and prompt deletion of any restored pilot files. Please provide dated written confirmations identifying the pilot files covered, when working copies were deleted, and when the last backup expired. If 45 days is a fixed backup cycle, please flag that as an outstanding exception for written agreement before transfer.

The schedule should name an incident contact and backup at each organization, with direct phone and email details. Please notify the archive contact within 24 hours of discovering suspected unauthorized access, disclosure, or loss, even if the investigation is ongoing.

We can consider one staged equipment photograph with a blank sheet. The frame must exclude donor material and identifying details, including anything visible on screens or labels. Publication requires separate written archive approval of the exact photograph, caption, and intended outlet. Signing the schedule grants no publication permission.

We can process the two restricted collections without studio staff viewing protected content if archive personnel handle any page placement that exposes handwriting or identifying details, along with all visual inspection and approval. Studio staff would configure and run the equipment with image previews disabled, apply the calibration, and perform automated checks. If a correction requires viewing a page or scan, archive personnel would inspect it and direct the rescan. Let’s confirm that workflow with a blank-sheet dry run before transfer.

The named specialist would start with the full-frame calibration sheet. If more examples are needed, we’d use only masked scans from other collections that the archive has checked and approved in writing. The specialist’s access would end as soon as calibration is complete or after three business days, whichever comes first. The studio would apply the calibration.

We accept the agreed ten-calendar-day review and correction periods and the two-business-day working-copy deletion deadline, including temporary files and specialist previews. Our backup rotation is fixed at 45 calendar days. We propose recording that as an exception for written agreement before transfer, with the final backup expiring within 45 calendar days of working-copy deletion. Backup access would be limited to disaster recovery, and we’d promptly delete any restored pilot files. We’d provide a dated working-copy deletion confirmation and a dated final backup expiry confirmation, each identifying the pilot files covered and the date the action occurred.

Before transfer, each organization would list its primary and backup incident contacts with direct phone numbers and email addresses. We’d notify the archive’s primary contact, or its backup if the primary is unavailable, within 24 hours of discovering suspected unauthorized access, disclosure, or loss, even while the investigation is ongoing.

We accept separate written approval for the exact staged photograph, caption, and intended outlet. The frame would contain a blank sheet and exclude donor material and identifying details, including on screens and labels. Publication would require that separate approval after the schedule is signed.

We agree to the restricted-collection workflow. Before transfer, we’ll run the blank-sheet test together to confirm that studio staff can operate the equipment with previews disabled and without seeing a page during placement, scanning, or removal. Archive personnel will handle exposed pages, perform visual checks, and direct any rescans. If the test reveals a step that exposes protected content, we’ll hold those two collections until we’ve corrected and retested it.

Please include the specialist controls as agreed. The archive must approve the named specialist in writing. The specialist may view the calibration sheet and, if needed, only masked scans from other collections that the archive has individually approved in writing. Access is view-only under written confidentiality and use restrictions, with downloads, local copies, and onward sharing disabled. Access ends on completion of calibration or after three business days, whichever comes first.

We accept the review, correction, and working-copy deletion terms as drafted. **The sole outstanding exception is the fixed 45-calendar-day backup rotation.** Please list it separately for express written archive approval before transfer, measured from working-copy deletion. The exception would cover disaster-recovery backups only, with prompt deletion of restored pilot files and dated, file-specific confirmations of both working-copy deletion and final backup expiry. We’ll hold transfer pending that approval.

Please include the agreed primary and backup incident contacts, direct contact details, and 24-hour notice from discovery of a suspected incident. The publicity clause should require separate written archive approval of the exact staged equipment photograph, caption, and outlet before publication, with only a blank sheet in the setup and no donor material or identifying details visible.

### Pilot confidentiality schedule

**Restricted collections.** Before transfer, the archive will identify the two restricted collections and both parties will run a blank-sheet test. The test must confirm that studio staff can operate the equipment with previews disabled and without seeing the page during placement, scanning, or removal. Archive personnel will handle exposed pages, perform visual checks, and direct any rescans. If the test reveals a step that would expose protected content, transfer of the two collections will wait until the parties correct the workflow and successfully retest it.

**Color calibration.** The archive must approve one named specialist in writing before access begins. The specialist may view the full-frame calibration sheet and, if needed, masked scans from other collections that the archive has checked for identifying content and approved individually in writing. Access is view-only in a secure workspace, with downloads, local copies, and onward sharing disabled. The specialist must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions. Access ends when calibration is complete or after three business days, whichever comes first. The studio will apply the calibration.

**Review, corrections, and working-copy deletion.** The archive has ten calendar days after delivery to report defects. The studio will deliver corrections within ten calendar days of receiving each timely defect report. The studio will delete all working copies, including temporary files and specialist previews, within two business days after the review window closes or the last timely correction is delivered, whichever is later.

**Backup exception requiring express written archive approval.** The studio requests approval for its fixed 45-calendar-day rotation, measured from working-copy deletion. The exception applies only to disaster-recovery backups. Access is limited to disaster recovery, any restored pilot files will be deleted promptly, and the final backup containing pilot files will expire within the 45-day period. The studio will provide separate dated written confirmations of working-copy deletion and final backup expiry, each identifying the pilot files covered and the date of deletion or expiry. Transfer will remain on hold until the archive expressly approves this exception in writing.

**Incident contacts and notice.** Before transfer, each party will enter the name, direct phone number, and email address of its primary and backup incident contacts in the schedule.

| Organization | Primary contact | Backup contact |
|---|---|---|
| Archive | [Name, direct phone, email] | [Name, direct phone, email] |
| Studio | [Name, direct phone, email] | [Name, direct phone, email] |

The studio will notify the archive’s primary contact, or its backup if the primary is unavailable, within 24 hours of discovering suspected unauthorized access, disclosure, or loss, even if the investigation is ongoing.

**Publicity.** The studio may submit one staged equipment photograph using a blank sheet. The frame must exclude donor material and identifying details, including anything visible on screens or labels. The studio may publish only after receiving separate written archive approval of the exact photograph, caption, and intended outlet.
